description: Vehicle read body rotation from the live prim after PhysX overwrote it; frozen spawn transient became a fake 14 deg rest tilt
evidence_quote: That frozen transient was then un-rotated from every attitude report ... PX4 then "levelled" an already-level vehicle: tilted thrust, wrong-frame rates, flip within ~2.5 s of liftoff
ruining_rationale: Uncaught, the vehicle flips within 2.5 s of every liftoff; on hardware that is a crash rather than a lost sim run.

description: mavros_interface mapped cmd->yaw_rate (which carries absolute yaw) into the attitude setpoint, giving PX4 a full-error yaw step during the ground thrust ramp
evidence_quote: PX4 received a full-error yaw step during the ground thrust ramp, saturated the mixer diagonals at sub-hover thrust and tipped the vehicle over its landing gear (measured 2026-07-28
ruining_rationale: Vehicle tips over its gear on every takeoff attempt; interpreting the field as a rate instead caused EKF divergence and a crash.

description: yaw_ and is_yaw_received_ were declared but never updated because mavros_odometry_sub_ was never created
evidence_quote: yaw_/is_yaw_received_ were declared but never updated - mavros_odometry_sub_ was never created.
ruining_rationale: Dead state field found alongside the yaw-step defect; no independent failure was attributed to it.

description: natnet_ros2 rigid-body id was not env-overridable, so adopting upstream's config reset it and the client silently dropped every mocap frame
evidence_quote: a stale id connects fine, creates the publishers, and then drops every frame. No external vision reaches EKF2 and the drone will not hold position or arm.
ruining_rationale: A silent total loss of external vision in the mocap room: the drone will not arm, ending the session before it starts.

description: Hummingbird e2e test read the Isaac scene marker immediately after the container reported Running, before a cold scene had written it
evidence_quote: a cold Isaac start - Kit, Pegasus, the flat-plane env, then the 45 MB drone USD - takes minutes, so the first run failed on a marker the scene had not written yet
ruining_rationale: A test-harness race that fails fast and cheaply; it does not consume a flight session.

description: Stale colcon CMake caches against numpy 2.x fail the build; the autonomy stack then never launches and the tmux pane shows only a prompt
evidence_quote: Stale colcon CMake caches vs numpy 2.x (2026-08-17): a failed `colcon build` means the autonomy stack never launches and the tmux pane just shows a prompt.
ruining_rationale: The note records it cost real hours; whether it would have surfaced mid-session depends on when the cache went stale.
fix_loc: n/a (documented defect, no isolated fix commit)

description: docker-compose VAR=${VAR:-} defined the drone USD path as empty string, so the scene loaded the stock Pegasus iris instead of the Hummingbird
evidence_quote: USE_HUMMINGBIRD went false and the scene loaded the stock Pegasus iris instead of hummingbird_grasp.usd. The failure was near-silent
ruining_rationale: Near-silent: everything downstream (claw, gripper, Teensy server) is absent, so a whole session is spent flying the wrong drone.

description: Pegasus attach_camera_to_drone hardcodes the iris body prim; the Hummingbird has none, so createJoint left body0 empty and welded all ZED cameras to the world origin
evidence_quote: An empty body0 means WORLD, so each camera was welded to the world origin.
ruining_rationale: Cameras are left behind when the drone flies; visible immediately, but it invalidates any perception data recorded in that session.

description: GCS Takeoff button defaulted to 10 m; the saved Foxglove layout overrode the extension default, so the panel kept sending 10 m
evidence_quote: Foxglove restores each panel's SAVED state over the extension default ... so the panel kept sending 10 m regardless
ruining_rationale: In a mocap room whose wire sits at ~2 m, a 10 m takeoff command flies the drone above the whole scene.

description: perch_task flew the world-frame latch point as if it were robot-frame, because PX4's local frame is boot-rooted rather than anchored by set_gps_origins
evidence_quote: the world-frame LATCH_POINT_M was being flown as if it were robot-frame, putting the target ~1.5 m wide of the wire
ruining_rationale: The drone flies 1.5 m wide of the conductor on every attempt, so no latch is possible and the cause is not visible from the task's own logs.

description: perch_task's airborne guard compared absolute altitude, but the landed body rests at z ~0.5 m, so the check passed on the ground
evidence_quote: MIN_AIRBORNE_Z_M was an absolute altitude, but the landed body sits at z ~0.5 in the world frame (spawn height + landing gear), so the check passed on the ground
ruining_rationale: A perch approach can be commanded on a grounded drone, which drives the airframe into the floor rather than the wire.

description: The commanded latch point was 2.00 m while the modelled conductor hangs near 1.86 m at that span position, a 0.14 m aim error
evidence_quote: ric_demo_powerline (span 4.0, height 2.0, sag 0.15) puts the conductor near z=1.86 at x=0.5, not 2.00 - about 0.14 m below where perch aims.
ruining_rationale: Documented as a known mismatch when introduced and reconciled later; on its own it prevents capture but is visible in one attempt.

description: action_relay's 5 m airborne gate rejected every perch goal, since the whole approach happens between 0.6 m and the wire at ~2 m
evidence_quote: "Takeoff first - drone is at 0.62m AGL (need >= 5m)." That is an outdoor number and it blocked perch outright
ruining_rationale: Perch can never be commanded at all; the gate can only be satisfied by flying above the thing being perched on.

description: teensy_serial opened its port once at startup and kept a deleted pty after socat respawned, so claw commands were written to nothing with no error
evidence_quote: it sat holding /dev/pts/3 (deleted) while /dev/ttyACM0 pointed at /dev/pts/4. Writes went nowhere, nothing was ever read, and no error appeared anywhere.
ruining_rationale: The claw silently stops responding after any Isaac restart, with no error at either end - the failure mode that motivated the whole investigation.

description: teensy_serial died at startup if the Isaac TCP server was not listening yet; socat's forever flag had been masking the start-up race
evidence_quote: socat's `forever` had been absorbing the start-up race ... so removing it exposed that the node dies if the far end is not listening yet
ruining_rationale: Bring-up order between the robot and sim containers is not guaranteed, so the node can fail to start at all.

description: teensy_serial test doubles desynced from the node: the stub exposed serial.Serial while the node called serial_for_url, and a raising fake spun the reconnect loop forever
evidence_quote: I committed the previous change with these red - my fault, and the failures were real rather than incidental
ruining_rationale: Test-suite breakage caught at the desk; it costs no flight session.

description: The gripper's one-shot open lost a race with articulation init, so the stiff USD drive slammed the jaw shut and auto_latch ratcheted it closed
evidence_quote: On a fresh scene the claw came up ST:0,0.0,LATCHED - jaw closed, already ratcheted, with nothing to latch onto.
ruining_rationale: The claw is closed before the flight begins, so every perch attempt in that session is wasted on an unusable gripper.

description: The fix for the start-open race re-asserted set_dof_position every tick, teleporting the jaw and feeding reaction torque into the airframe while PX4's EKF initialised
evidence_quote: repeating it snapped the jaw back each step, and the reaction torque went into the airframe at exactly the moment PX4's EKF was initialising ... Takeoff degraded as a result.
ruining_rationale: A regression that degrades every takeoff while looking like a flight-control problem, not a gripper problem.

description: Five documented HUMMINGBIRD_* scene knobs were never forwarded into the isaac-sim container, so setting them in an overrides env file did nothing
evidence_quote: five documented knobs were silently inert when set in an overrides/*.env
ruining_rationale: A/B levers appear to be set but are inert, so experiments silently test the same configuration twice.

description: PX4_PHYSICS_HZ was 100 while the PX4 lockstep backend ran at 250 Hz, so PX4 integrated against a plant stepping 2.5x slower than it expects
evidence_quote: PX4 was integrating against a plant stepping 2.5x slower than it expects
ruining_rationale: Contributes about half the hover attitude ripple; it degrades every flight rather than aborting one.

description: The motor model defaulted to a freewheel deceleration identified on a bench rig with the ESC brake off, while the flight ESCs brake regeneratively
evidence_quote: the bench measured the coast "with the KDE ESC's brake off" and that the real mode "depends on the FLIGHT ESC config" - so freewheel was a bench-rig artifact
ruining_rationale: Dominant phase term at the limit cycle, but the correction was reasoned from a datasheet rather than triggered by a failed run.

description: waypoint_planner rejected TakeoffTask when the drone was not armed instead of arming it, so the GCS Takeoff button aborted on the PX4-position deployment
evidence_quote: [relay] /robot_1/tasks/takeoff: ABORTED ... Cause: waypoint_planner rejected with "not armed" instead of arming.
ruining_rationale: The only takeoff control in the demo path does nothing, and the author's own test scripts armed beforehand so the GCS path was never exercised.

description: waypoint_planner's launch file was missing the robot_command remap, so the client resolved under the node namespace and never reached the interface service
evidence_quote: The launch file was also missing the robot_command remap, so the client would have resolved under the node namespace and never reached /$ROBOT_NAME/interface/robot_command
ruining_rationale: Arming commands go to a name nothing serves, which reproduces the dead-button symptom even after the logic fix.

description: _abandon() took a non-reentrant lock and then called _pose(), which takes it again, deadlocking the action thread and stopping the cmd_pose stream mid-flight
evidence_quote: the action thread deadlocked holding _task_lock, _tick() blocked, cmd_pose stopped streaming and PX4 would drop OFFBOARD ~0.5 s later - mid-flight. This already fired
ruining_rationale: PX4 drops OFFBOARD roughly 0.5 s after the deadlock while airborne; it had already fired once as an unexplained rejected land goal.

description: action_relay read altitude from NavSatFix while this deployment runs with GPS off, so its altitude stayed None and perch was rejected permanently
evidence_quote: current_z stayed None so perch was rejected with "no GPS fix yet" forever, no matter what the planner did
ruining_rationale: Perch is unreachable from the GCS regardless of what the planner does, and the error message points at GPS rather than the gate.

description: Takeoff failed on the first press after bring-up, with no state estimate then failed to arm, because PX4 will not arm before EKF2 converges
evidence_quote: Takeoff failed on the first press after bring-up two different ways: instantly, with "no state estimate", and later with "failed to arm" - PX4 refuses to arm until EKF2 converges on vision, which takes minutes here.
ruining_rationale: Costs the first attempt of every session; recoverable by waiting, but it masquerades as a hard failure.

description: The world-to-robot conversion added earlier became wrong once PX4 ran external-vision-only, and would have sent the drone 1.5 m past the wire
evidence_quote: Applying them sends the drone to world (0.0, 1.5, 1.648): 1.5 m past the wire on the far side.
ruining_rationale: The same 1.5 m miss as the original frame defect, this time introduced by the earlier fix rather than by the original code.

description: MPC_Z_VEL_MAX_UP was taken from a single unrepresentative flight log at 0.2, which makes PX4's smooth-takeoff ramp charge its integrator backwards
evidence_quote: hummingbird.env was built from 19_29_59.ulg, one of those 5, whose own takeoff was in STAB with a 0.23 m hop - a fine source for the attitude gains, a poor one for a takeoff parameter.
ruining_rationale: Takeoff takes 41 s instead of ~13 s; expensive in session time but not destructive.

description: THR_MDL_FAC was unset in sim while the real aircraft flew 0.30, manufacturing an apparent 17 percent hover-thrust deficit that distorted other measurements
evidence_quote: The sim was the one running PX4's default of 0, so setting it is a fidelity CORRECTION ... That deficit was never a modelling error in the thrust curve; it was a missing parameter.
ruining_rationale: It had been distorting measurements all session and drove investigation toward the thrust curve, which was correct.

description: LinearDrag was inherited from the 1.52 kg iris as an absolute coefficient, giving the 8.8 kg airframe a nearly undamped translational plant
evidence_quote: Carried onto 8.784 kg it gives K = b/m = 0.057 1/s, six times below the bottom of the 0.1-0.6 1/s range the rotorcraft literature gives
ruining_rationale: Leading explanation for the horizontal limit cycle, but the commit's own measurement could neither confirm nor refute the change.

description: Tying the settle hold to the tight arrival radius made the drone start the attach leg from rest, stalling the route for 60 s
evidence_quote: Flown, that made perch WORSE: the drone settled stationary under the wire, began the ascent from rest, and stalled on the attach leg for 60 s where the same route had previously succeeded.
ruining_rationale: A regression that turned a previously succeeding perch route into a 60 s stall, discovered only by flying it.

description: Bench-identified motor lag included the rig's own command chain, so the sim carried roughly twice the real command-to-torque lag
evidence_quote: the bench's 31 ms deadtime + 40 ms tau_up identified the rig's command chain along with the motor
ruining_rationale: Doubled actuator lag drove a limit cycle that was investigated as a controller-tuning problem for several sessions.

description: The motor_model module self-test still assumed the freewheel default and had been failing silently since the symmetric default landed
evidence_quote: Also fixes the module self-test, which still assumed the default decel mode is freewheel (broken silently since the symmetric default landed).
ruining_rationale: A stale self-test found at the desk; no flight time is at risk.

description: action_relay latched its ground reference from the first odometry sample delivered when its executor began spinning, which was mid-climb
evidence_quote: Measured consequence 2026-08-25: ground latched at 0.69 m mid-climb, so a 1.0 m hover read 0.31 m AGL and perch was rejected with 'Takeoff first'.
ruining_rationale: Perch is rejected after a successful takeoff, and a relay restarted mid-flight is poisoned the same way.

description: Routes drove the body centre rather than the claw pivot, which is mounted 7.5 cm off-centre in y, so the jaw closed beside the conductor
evidence_quote: the route now targets y=-0.075 so the jaw, not the body centre, aligns with the conductor (three historical attempts closed 7.5 cm beside the wire)
ruining_rationale: Three separate flight attempts closed the claw next to the wire; each attempt costs a full bring-up and flight.

description: The USD authored the sensing jaw's spring with a preload far above what a slack wire can exert, so the depression signal could never fire
evidence_quote: The slack ric-demo wire pushes back with 0.06-0.8 N (~0.05 N*m at the jaw), so DEP could never fire - verified through visually-confirmed wire-in-jaw contact.
ruining_rationale: The wire was visibly inside the jaw and capture still never triggered, which is indistinguishable from an approach-geometry failure.

description: Two goal handlers spinning the relay's single executor concurrently lost futures, so an unresolved takeoff starved every later goal at wait_for_server
evidence_quote: a takeoff whose result never resolves then starves every later goal at wait_for_server/send (observed twice - perch goals logged but never forwarded)
ruining_rationale: Observed twice: perch goals are logged as received and then silently never forwarded, stalling the session.

description: Perch hang classification used a z floor, so a flyaway caused by wire recoil was classified as a successful hang
evidence_quote: the AUTO.LAND descent slid the latched claw into the pole and the wire's elastic recoil slung the drone to 22 m - and the z >= z_latch - 0.75 floor check happily classified that flyaway as HANGING
ruining_rationale: The system reports success while the drone is 22 m away; on hardware this is an uncontained flyaway.

description: The propeller spin writer rotated empty hub marker Xforms rather than the visible propeller meshes, so nothing ever moved on screen
evidence_quote: The spin writer has been rotating <airframe>/rotor{i} all along - empty hub marker Xforms, so nothing ever moved on screen.
ruining_rationale: Cosmetic only; no physics or control behaviour depends on the visual.

description: natnet_ros2 does not re-register with a new scene's NatNet server after a warm Isaac relaunch, leaving mocap silent and arming denied
evidence_quote: natnet_ros2 does NOT re-register with a new scene's NatNet server after a warm relaunch (measured - optitrack silent, arming denied)
ruining_rationale: Warm relaunch is the fast iteration loop; without the rule every mocap flight after a relaunch fails to arm for no visible reason.

description: A launch param file loaded with allow_substs is evaluated as raw text including comments, so a comment mentioning a substitution aborts the launch
evidence_quote: `<param from="x.yaml" allow_substs="true"/>` evaluates the YAML's RAW TEXT including comments - a comment mentioning `$(var sim)` aborts the launch.
ruining_rationale: Aborts bring-up from a code comment, which is not a place anyone looks first.
fix_loc: n/a (documented defect, no isolated fix commit)

description: The snapshot hook pumps bare app.update() calls that step physics while the timeline is playing; recorded as unfixed
evidence_quote: The snapshot hook (`HUMMINGBIRD_SNAP_*`) pumps bare app.update() calls that STEP PHYSICS while playing ... unfixed as of 2026-08-27
ruining_rationale: Corrupts the physics of any run that has snapshots enabled, which is the visual-review configuration.
fix_loc: n/a (documented defect, no isolated fix commit)

description: The NatNet emulator's SIGINT handler hangs Kit shutdown, so a warm scene relaunch requires a forced kill and a wait for the prompt
evidence_quote: the NatNet emulator's SIGINT handler hangs Kit shutdown: send C-c, wait ~10 s, then `pkill -9 -f ...`
ruining_rationale: Costs iteration time during relaunch; it does not corrupt a flight already in progress.
fix_loc: n/a (documented defect, no isolated fix commit)

description: Restarting only the robot container against an already-used Isaac scene causes EKF runaway, with altitude diverging to about 19 m
evidence_quote: robot-only restarts on a used scene cause EKF runaway (z -> 19 m)
ruining_rationale: The estimator diverges to 19 m while the drone is nominally hovering, which ends the session and can end the airframe.
fix_loc: n/a (documented defect, no isolated fix commit)

description: The disarm PWM step into the braking KDE ESCs is the source of the real-drone Jetson brownout; no PX4 parameter softens it
evidence_quote: The disarm PWM step (working -> PWM_MAIN_DIS in one cycle) into braking KDE ESCs is the real-drone Jetson brownout source
ruining_rationale: The onboard computer browns out on disarm on the real aircraft, taking down logging and autonomy at the end of every flight.
fix_loc: n/a (documented defect, no isolated fix commit)

description: The landing gear mass was an unmeasured 0.450 kg guess; weighed, it is 626.7 g, so the model was 28 percent light
evidence_quote: John weighed it. The 0.450 kg default was never measured ... It was 28% light.
ruining_rationale: A mass-model error that biases hover-thrust reasoning; it was corroborated from logs rather than discovered by a failed flight.
